newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close lower, hold above 800 on AEX.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close lower, hold above 800 on AEX.

text.p: Dutch shares finished lower on Thursday, retreating from Wednesday's record high close on light profit-taking prompted by a weaker bond market performance and an early decline on Wall Street.

The AEX share index held onto the bulk of Wednesday's 16.48 point gain to finish 3.09 points down at 800.84. The index set a new intra-day record of 807.98 in early business -- beating Wednesday's 806.01 peak -- boosted by stock shortages.
"When you look at how much the index went up yesterday and then see how little of that it gave away today you have to be impressed by how strong sentiment is," a dealer said.
Dealers said the market was still basking in the glow of Tuesday's decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve to leave interest rates unchanged at its Open Market Committee meeting.

"There's a very positive feeling in the market, we've not had too many disappointments from company results, apart from KLM and Nedlloyd yesterday, we can see this market going up to 820-822 pretty soon," a dealer said.

Some analysts are predicting the AEX index can advance to to 830 in the next week or so with technical analysts advising clients to buy dips as longer term prospects are good. One chart analyst is forecasting 875 as a 12-month target.

Not everyone agrees with the prospect of endlessly continuing advances, with one or two becoming nervous about the prospects for domestic inflation, particularly after figures early on Thursday showing a fall in Dutch unemployment.
Joblessness in February to April fell to 399,000, against 465,000 a year earlier, government figures showed.

"Unemployment below 400,000 starts to look like full employment and when you get that situation it inevitably puts upward pressure on wages and that's a major element in the Dutch inflation outlook," said a dealer. His view was that the market could drop to around 600 if interest rates trended higher.
